concept: Prism ML ternary Hadamard-rotated weights kernel on Metal
summary: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B weights are rotated blockwise by an orthogonal Hadamard transform (block 1024, fixed plus/minus 1 signs) before ternary assignment, and the runtime applies the matching transform to activations

facts.text: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B weights are rotated blockwise by an orthogonal Hadamard transform (block 1024, fixed plus/minus 1 signs) before ternary assignment, and the runtime applies the matching transform to activations
The rotation is folded into the stored weights offline and costs no extra bits or weight traffic
The packed model declares its rotation as metadata so a runtime must apply the matching transform or refuse to load
Ordinary MLX loaders skip the activation transform and the inverse embedding lookup and return wrong output rather than an error
The weight format is ternary g128 with one FP16 scale per 128 weights, about 1.71 bits per weight, 1.72 for the whole language model
MLX stores the ternary levels as 2-bit codes with scale s and bias -s, which costs 2.25 bits per weight against 2.13 for PQ2_0
The MLX pack is 8.60 GB: 7.67 GB language model plus a 0.92 GB unquantized FP16 vision tower that needs no rotation
26.2M parameters (0.0976 percent of the language model) stay in higher precision
Two GGUF packings exist: PTQ1_0 at 5.95 GB and PQ2_0 at 7.21 GB, and neither is uniformly faster across GPUs
The model card's M5 Pro Metal row (llama.cpp fork, PQ2_0) is 28.1 tok/s TG128 and 387 tok/s PP512 with decode streaming about 204 GB/s of weights and drawing 27.5 W on the GPU rail
Earlier pre-rotation Apple numbers: M5 Max 47.0 TG128 and 765 PP512, M4 Pro 18.0 TG128 and 125 PP512, all at 7.2 GB
Stock llama.cpp cannot run the Bonsai 2 GGUF packs; the PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp fork is required
Prism ML states 1.76 effective bits, 5.9 GB, 98.2 percent aggregate retention (83.9 against 85.4 for Qwen3.8 27B) and 46.8 tok/s on M5 Max
The announcement is dated 2026-09-17 and says the first Ternary Bonsai 27B retained about 95 percent
